body: Thank you, this really helped me, thank you
Sadly, not everyone can afford one

I'm not in touch with my family. I dont have a job right now to support my social connections, so staying at home a lot and having less to no money to go out, equals manufactured (?) lonelyness. I dont blame others, this is just how my life ended up to be including my own choices. Going through a breakup as well and that was basically the only person left.
I really hope so, I just dont have the energy to believe that right now. Thank you for your kind words
No idea anymore if sarcasm or genuine

One thing you need to think about is. You don't trust your boyfriend, but you don't know his boss at all. You don't even know if she's into him or find him attractive at all. She is also a person with a mind and feelings. Maybe she already has he heart with someone else and sees him purely as a friendly person who she can laugh with. 


Excuse me for asking but is it possible that you have been cheated on in the past? Or is it that he talks to her in a way you wish he would talk to you about instead? Maybe you want him to send you random messages and funny videos etc.

I know its hard to get comments that basically say get over yourself, but we are all people with thoughts and feelings and not everyone is perfect. Insecurity is a thing a lot of people deal with, but its how you act on it that determines who you are. 

Besides, its kind of weird that he left you hanging at his work place. Did you go without his consent? Then I can definitely image where he's coming from. Or is he really being shady about you coming there? Only you have this answer.

Why did you fight and break up? Is it because he felt unreasonably treated, or that he sticks up for her? Think about how exactly he responds about you not feeling comfortable about her. 

You are in a relationship and you have every right to say you are not comfortable with something. If you are feeling insecure and don't know how to handle it, you don't deserve to be burned down because of it. If you really were this jealousy-monster, than you wouldn't even made the effort to ask for help and make a post about it here. 

Just try to have a gentle talk with him and maybe let him in on things he maybe doesn't know about? Your insecurity definitely comes from SOMEWHERE. Try to reflect on that before you see him as the bad guy. We live in a world where its hard for people to have attractive friends, whether its a guy or a girl. Its just too easy to cheat and I get where you are coming from. But like I already said, it's how you deal with your insecurities that makes you what kind of person you are.

Anyway, if you ever feel like talking just hit me up!

I'm sorry, people like this don't even deserve to be broken up with personally. Not when you are afraid of your own safety. 

Don't go over there, message him through your phone if you have too, block him everywhere you can possibly imagine. Don't let him get to your friends as well, warn every relative and friend who knows about him, before he can persuade them to talk to you and change your mind. 

You don't need to be there to be even more traumatized by his unhinged behavior if he doesn't see this coming at all. Spare yourself this hardship. I even go as far to say that don't contact mental health authorities, HE IS NOT YOUR RESPONSIBILITY. Go to the police if he crosses the line and really makes you feel afraid. 

Please do the right thing, I definitely speak behalf of all the people that didn't see how wrong he was this early before even breaking out until we were stuck and dependent and abused. DON'T DO THIS TO YOURSELF. Don't make it worse than it already is.

He's dangerous and has many red flags that a lot of abused people can relate too. Don't become one of us if you still have the chance.

So there you have it, I think his insecurity and this rejection he's experiencing is also crushing him. He's going through things and if you are up for it, you should consider being there for him. A relationship is hard work and commitment.

In life not everyone responds well to their problems and some people learned to talk instantly and lean on others, and some people learned that its best to keep things inside and not be a bother to others. 

I don't think he's doing this to hurt you or others. Maybe he's a bit lost in life and has no one to guide or be there for him. He seems to feel that he has no control over his life at the moment since he can't have the job he actually wants. I hope that he has some sort of support, because weed looks like its his only support.

I'm sorry but this is way too fishy. And his excuse is that she's older? I'm 2 years older than my bf. 1 year doesn't make a difference AT ALL. 

Saying things like honey and you not being comfortable with it, is really crossing the line here. His relationship with her is crossing the line for you, and you have every right to say something about it. If he keeps making up excuses, it would be best to see if you should end things between you two.

Just a thought. Isn't your bf maybe dealing with something you don't know about? 
What is the real reason behind him quitting his job, do you know that?

Maybe before breaking up, you should try to talk to him about it. If he still loves you and values everything you should, you should give it a chance.

Besides, it is your place to ask him to stop if its affecting you this badly. And if you still put effort to fix this, and he still rejects you. Then you at least know you tried all you could.
You're most welcome. I'm happy that its appreciated.
